subject: AI & Agents
title: Sora: Text to Video
description: A micro-lesson that makes Sora: Text to Video usable.

hook.text: A woman walks through neon-lit Tokyo streets. Every detail is photorealistic. Every frame is AI-generated.

buildup.text: OpenAI's Sora generates up to 60 seconds of high-definition video from text prompts.

discovery.text: It models videos as sequences of spacetime patches, extending diffusion from 2D images to 3D video.

twist.text: Physical inconsistencies remain — a glass shatters but reassembles, gravity shifts mid-scene.

climax.text: The film and advertising industries face a fundamental question: what becomes of video production?

punchline.text: From text to moving pictures. Cinema's next revolution.

quiz.question: What does OpenAI's Sora generate?
options: Only still images from video input

details.summary: OpenAI's Sora generates realistic minute-long videos from text descriptions, creating coherent scenes with consistent characters, physics, and camera movements that were unthinkable just years earlier.
details.whyItMatters: Text-to-video represents the next frontier in generative AI. It has profound implications for filmmaking, advertising, education, and also for the potential creation of convincing misinformation.
takeaways: Sora generates realistic videos from text descriptions alone
It maintains scene consistency across many seconds of video
The technology has huge implications for media and misinformation

faq.question: How does Sora generate videos from text?
faq.answer: Sora uses a diffusion transformer model that operates on spacetime patches of video. It generates video frames maintaining temporal consistency, physics, and character identity from text instructions.

faq.question: What are the risks of text-to-video AI?
faq.answer: Convincing fabricated videos could fuel misinformation and political manipulation. The technology makes it increasingly difficult to distinguish real footage from AI-generated content, threatening trust in video evidence.
